target_customer: Digital analytics, paid media and compliance teams and agencies that depend on tracking data from websites and apps
problem: Analytics and marketing tags break silently, so reports and ad spend rest on bad data. Trackingplan monitors real traffic to find broken tags, missing properties and consent breaches.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription with a free trial and an agency partner program

founders.name: Alexandros Andre Chaaraoui
founders.background_notes: YC page: worked at Google on Android computer vision and Assistant NLP; led an ML team at Rohde & Schwarz.

founders.name: Jose Padilla
founders.background_notes: YC page: builds software from desktop apps to home automation.

founders.name: Jose Luis Perez
founders.background_notes: YC page says he founded three tech companies and cites Techstars.

founders.name: Pedro Trujillano
founders.background_notes: YC page: founded three companies, business and technical, VC experience.

competitors.name: Avo
competitors.what: Event data governance with a tracking plan and Inspector that compares live data to the plan
competitors.traction_then: Product existed with Segment integration; scale not stated

competitors.name: Segment Protocols
competitors.what: Data governance add on that validates events flowing through Segment
competitors.traction_then: Part of Segment Business plans; sees only data Segment carries

technical_complexity.rationale: Discovering and validating traffic to 170+ vendors through tag manager or one line install is standard engineering with hard schema inference parts.

defensibility.rationale: Learned schemas and alert workflows create some lock in, but tracking QA tools were already offered by incumbents.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Platforms offered governance for their own data only; Trackingplan remains independent and claims 756+ customers on its site.

market_need_then: Companies rely on analytics and ad tags for decisions and consent compliance and broken tracking was a known cost, which created demand for QA tooling.

branding.name_origin: The company blog says the name matches the product and the central concept, since the tracking plan is the reference for a company's data collection.

identity.voice_and_tone: Trust and data quality; manifesto line says you cannot trust an agent that does not know when your data is wrong

branding.community_and_virality: Appears at MeasureCamp events in Spain and Italy and runs an agency partner directory.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name that is easy to understand but generic; community presence limited to analytics events and partners.

outcome_analysis: Trackingplan is a Barcelona company with a technical and entrepreneurial founding team that pre-seeded in 2021 with Spanish funds and angels and joined YC in winter 2022. It claims over 750 customers including large agencies and has repositioned as a digital analytics agent. No later priced round, exit or layoffs were found, so growth is capital efficient or undisclosed.
notes: The company blog says it has five founders; YC page lists four, only those four are named. The Nordic9 page lists total investment of 500K and a round value of N/A, so the amount is left null. CB Insights lists a 0.5M convertible note on 2022-03-29 (aggregator, unverified); Startup-Seeker claims 2.5M and Extruct 125K, both unverified. Competitor pages were found undated; incumbents named existed before the batch per the company's own comparison pages, so source_date is null.
